sources.note: Describes another variety (Glottolog tran1289). Table of contents + review read: reconstructs Continental Celtic word ACCENT as an expiratory stress whose position is inferred from 'stress-position indicators' (syncope, vowel centralization/narrowing, gemination/degemination, epenthesis, loss of -w-, nasal effacement; ch. IV), argues against a Common-Celtic initial stress (II.2.1) and for an archaic antepenultimate stress shifting to the penult (II.2.3, II.2.5); premise (p. 3, quoted by Darling) that no accent marks were ever written in Celtic sources and all Continental varieties are extinct…
